title: Prepositional: Exceptions & Edge Cases
titleRussian: Предложный падеж: исключения и особые случаи
description: Beyond the -е rule: the stressed locative -у/-ю (в лесу́, на полу́), soft-sign masculines and 3rd-declension feminines (о словаре, о матери), and the idiomatic на-collocations (на работе, на почте).
descriptionRussian: За пределами правила «-е»: ударное местное окончание -у́/-ю́ (в лесу́, на полу́), мягкий знак у мужских и третье склонение у женских (о словаре, о матери) и идиоматические сочетания с «на» (на работе, на почте).
intro: A handful of very common words do not follow the endings you have just learned. The strangest group takes one ending for being somewhere and a different ending for being talked about, so the same word has two shapes depending on the job it is doing. None of this is derivable. These are words you learn one at a time, and they are worth it.
rules: Special locative -у́ / -ю́: a closed set of common masculine nouns takes a stressed -у́ (-ю́ after a soft stem) after в or на when the meaning is purely 'where.' Examples: в лесу́, в саду́, на полу́, в шкафу́, на берегу́, в году́, в Крыму́, в порту́. After other prepositions, including о, the same noun takes the regular -е.

The same noun can split: locational в лесу́ (in the forest) vs topical о ле́се (about the forest). The job of the case picks the ending. Locational meaning after в/на = -у́; everywhere else = regular -е.
3rd-declension feminine: feminine nouns ending in a soft -ь take -и in the prepositional, not -е. Тетрадь → о тетради, ночь → о ночи, кровать → на кровати, площадь → на площади.

Мать and дочь add a stem extension -ер- before the ending in every case except nominative and accusative: о матери, о дочери. The -и ending is the regular 3rd-declension feminine ending; the extra -ер- is what makes these two stand out.

Idiomatic на-collocations: a small set of place-and-event words takes на where English speakers expect в. Memorize them as fixed phrases: на работе, на почте, на стадионе, на концерте, на уроке, на вокзале, на заводе. The case ending on the noun is regular; only the preposition is the exception.
examples: Маша в лесу́. (Masha is in the forest.) лес → в лесу́, special locative -у́.
Книга о ле́се. (A book about the forest.) лес → о ле́се, regular -е because the meaning is topical.
Кот на полу́. (The cat is on the floor.) пол → на полу́, special locative -у́.
Антон работает в саду́. (Anton works in the garden.) сад → в саду́.
Они отдыхают в Крыму́. (They are vacationing in Crimea.) Крым → в Крыму́.
Я пишу о тетради. (I am writing about the notebook.) тетрадь → о тетради, 3rd-declension feminine + -и.
Мы говорим о матери. (We are talking about mother.) мать → о матери, stem extension -ер- + -и.
Маша на работе. (Masha is at work.) работа → на работе, idiomatic на.
Антон на почте. (Anton is at the post office.) почта → на почте, idiomatic на.

tables.title: Special locative -у́ / -ю́ (after в / на, locational only)
3rd-declension feminine: -ь → -и (plus the мать / дочь stem extension)
Idiomatic на-collocations (regular -е on the noun; на on the preposition)

items.hint: Лес is one of the special-locative masculines. After в meaning 'where,' what stressed ending appears?
items.explanation: Лес belongs to the closed special-locative set. After в or на with a purely locational meaning, it takes stressed -у́: в лесу́.

items.promptEnglish: The cat is on the floor.
items.hint: Same family as лес: stressed -у́ for location.
items.explanation: Пол is special-locative. After на with the meaning 'where,' it takes stressed -у́: на полу́.

items.hint: The meaning here is topical, not locational. Which ending fits?
items.explanation: When the meaning is 'about' rather than 'where,' лес takes the regular -е: о ле́се. The special -у́ ending is reserved for locational в / на.

items.hint: Мать is 3rd-declension feminine. What ending appears, and what extension is added?
items.explanation: Мать is 3rd-declension feminine. The prepositional ending is -и (not -е), and мать adds the stem extension -ер- before that ending: о матери.

items.promptEnglish: I am thinking about the notebook.
items.hint: Тетрадь ends in -ь and is feminine. Which case ending do 3rd-declension feminines take?
items.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in soft -ь are 3rd-declension. They take -и in the prepositional, not -е: тетрадь → о тетради. No stem extension is added: that twist applies only to мать and дочь.

items.hint: Работа takes the standard fem -а → -е ending. The lesson here is the preposition choice, not the ending.
items.explanation: Russian says на работе, not в работе, even though English speakers expect 'in.' The noun ending is regular (работа → работе, fem -а → -е). The exception is on the preposition side: работа joins the small set of place-and-event nouns that take на.

items.hint: Крым is on the special-locative list. After в meaning 'where,' which ending?
items.explanation: Крым is one of the geographic names in the special-locative set. After в with locational meaning, it takes stressed -у́: в Крыму́.

items.hint: Завод is in the на-collocation set. The case ending is regular masculine + -е.
items.explanation: Завод is a member of the idiomatic на-set (workplace). The case ending stays regular (masculine + -е): на заводе. Same form as в магазине, only the preposition differs.

items.hint: Дочь pairs with мать: 3rd-declension feminine plus the stem extension.
items.explanation: Дочь behaves exactly like мать: it is 3rd-declension feminine, so the prepositional ending is -и, and it adds the stem extension -ер-: о дочери. These two are the only nouns in everyday Russian that add the -ер- extension.

minimalPairs.explanation: After в with locational meaning, лес takes the special stressed -у́: в лесу́. The regular ле́се appears only in the topical meaning ('about the forest').

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Lena works at the post office.
minimalPairs.explanation: Почта belongs to the small set of place words that take на in Russian, even though English speakers expect 'in.' Russians say на почте, на работе, на стадионе. The case ending on the noun (-е) is fully regular; only the preposition is the exception.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The clothes are in the wardrobe.
errorCorrection.explanation: Шкаф belongs to the special-locative set: after locational в it takes the stressed ending -у́, giving в шкафу́. The regular -е form шка́фе is not used for plain location with this noun.

Сад is one of the closed set of masculine nouns that take the stressed special locative -у́ after в or на when the meaning is purely 'where': в саду́. The regular -е form is not used for plain location.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The key is in the door.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дверь is feminine and ends in a soft -ь, so it is 3rd-declension. 3rd-declension feminines take -и in the prepositional, not -е: в двери. Двере applies the regular fem -а → -е pattern to a noun that does not follow it.

Осень is a 3rd-declension feminine (soft -ь), so its prepositional ending is -и: об осени. (Осень starts with a vowel, so 'about' takes the form об, as Lesson 5 taught.) The bare осень is the nominative, left undeclined.

Работа is one of the idiomatic на-collocations: Russians say на работе for 'at work', never в работе for the location. The ending (-е) is already correct; работа is a regular fem -а → -е noun. The exception is the preposition: certain workplaces and event-places take на where English speakers expect 'in' (на работе, на почте, на стадионе). The phrase в работе does exist, but it is an idiom meaning 'in progress' ('проект в работе', the project is in the works), not a location.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We met at the train station.
errorCorrection.explanation: Вокзал belongs to the small set of transit and workplace nouns that take на where English speakers expect в: на вокзале. Learners pick в because вокзал is a building, but Russian groups it with на работе, на почте, на стадионе. The noun ending itself is regular (masculine + -е); only the preposition is the exception.

patternRecognition.question: Which exception pattern is at work?
options: Special locative -у́ after locational в / на
patternRecognition.answer: Special locative -у́ after locational в / на
patternRecognition.explanation: Крым is a member of the small set of common masculines (mostly one-syllable words) that take stressed -у́ when meaning 'where.' This is the special locative pattern: в Крыму́.

patternRecognition.question: Which exception pattern is at work?
patternRecognition.explanation: Дочь is feminine and ends in soft -ь, putting it in the 3rd declension. The prepositional ending is -и (not -е), and дочь is one of only two nouns in everyday Russian (with мать) that add the stem extension -ер- before that ending: дочь → о дочери.

patternRecognition.question: Why is this an exception, and where exactly?
options: The preposition choice is irregular; the noun ending is normal
The case is wrong; it should be accusative
patternRecognition.answer: The preposition choice is irregular; the noun ending is normal
patternRecognition.explanation: Стадион ends in a hard consonant and takes the standard masculine + -е: стадионе. There is nothing irregular about the noun form. The irregularity is purely on the preposition side: Russian groups стадион with concert venues and other event-places that all take на, where English speakers expect 'in.'

patternRecognition.question: Which exception pattern is at work?
options: Special locative -у́ after locational в / на
patternRecognition.answer: Special locative -у́ after locational в / на
patternRecognition.explanation: Пол belongs to the closed special-locative set. After на with locational meaning, it takes stressed -у́: на полу́. The preposition choice itself is unsurprising (пол is a surface, and surfaces take на), but the case ending on the noun is the exception.

reviewVocab.definition: the textbook example of the special locative. Stressed -у́ after locational в / на; regular -е after topical о.
reviewVocab.example: Маша в лесу́, и она пишет книгу о ле́се.

reviewVocab.definition: 3rd-declension feminine + stem extension -ер- + -и. Дочь behaves the same way.
reviewVocab.example: Я думаю о матери и о дочери.

reviewVocab.definition: idiomatic на-collocation. The noun ending is regular (работа → работе); the preposition choice is the exception.
